sections.title: Blackness in Latin America, an Introduction
sections.description: This course offers an overview of the history, experiences, and subjectivities of Africans and their descendants in Latin America. It begins by considering perceptions of Africans in Antiquity; it succinctly explores the Kingdom of Kongo, the early stages of enslavement in the Iberian Peninsula, the expansion of the Trans-Atlantic Trade of African captives, the Middle Passage, enslavement, independence movements, early republicanism, to the present. The course traces the strategies African and Afro-descendant social actors implemented to evade, maneuver, resist, and undo enslavement and discrimination, as well as the processes of race-making in the region. The course explores the methodological challenges of studying and writing the history of people who did not have access to literacy and whose voices, philosophy, and contributions remain disavowed and sidelined. The course is organized chronologically and thematically. We will READ and analyze primary and secondary sources to underscore some of the contributions the African Diaspora has given to the Americas and the world, as well as the debates that continue shaping Africana/African Diaspora studies.
